messages:
Customer Joe: Hey team — since the protobuf framing change rolled yesterday we started getting customer reports of huge p99 for streaming responses. Non-stream endpoints look normal. Observed: TTFB jumps from ~50ms to 450-800ms for some requests, total time unaffected for the same payload when using non-streaming. Request-id: rq_8f3b2a. Model: redwood/gpt-small-v1 (hosted).

Jamie S: Thanks Joe — can you paste a minimal repro curl and the exact endpoint+headers? Also need the request-id/time window to pull that trace.

Customer Joe: repro below (sanitized):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-small-v1","prompt":"hello","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/complete
```
Happens on ~10% of streams in europe region after 14:23 UTC. sample rq ids: rq_8f3b2a, rq_8f3b3c, rq_8f3b90

Jamie S: Got it. Pulling traces now. @sre-bot can you attach any deploys or infra events around 2025-12-09 14:20-14:40 UTC?

sre-bot: deploy-bot posted: "canary deploy: runtime-protobuf-framing v2.1.0 rolled to europe-canary at 2025-12-09T14:18:07Z"

Maria L: thanks — that matches. quick summary of what we've seen from telemetry: p99 TTFB for streaming jumped in europe-canary from 120ms -> ~520ms; non-stream p99 stable. Metrics show increased queueing at edge proxies right before first chunk.

Chris H: I pulled a packet capture for rq_8f3b2a. Observed pattern: service generates first chunk quickly, but client doesn't receive it until a ~400ms gap. The payload size of the first chunk increased (~+8 bytes) due to new varint length prefix from protobuf framing. This seems to trigger coalescing in the upstream HTTP/2 proxy.

Maria L: yup — reproducer locally: when chunk payload is small (~120B) + new 2-3 byte frame header, the proxy's flush heuristics + Nagle-type behavior (socket coalesce) cause an extra flush delay. Non-stream path uses larger frames so it's unaffected.

Jamie S: Possible mitigations? Customer wants a workaround ASAP.

Maria L: Options (short term):
- rollback canary (v2.1.0) — will remove proto framing change, fixes immediately but loses framing perf benefits
- edge feature-flag: disable protobuf length-prefix for streaming (server side) — needs tiny patch, low-risk, canary-able
- force immediate tcp flush on first-chunk path (setsockopt/TCP_NODELAY) — riskier on throughput

Chris H: Additional quick hack: pad first chunk to >200B so proxy doesn't coalesce (server-side pad 80-100 bytes). Very low-risk, quick to ship as a config toggle.

Jamie S: Which is fastest to get to customers?

Maria L: pad-first-chunk toggle or edge FF to disable length-prefix. Pad toggle can be pushed to europe canary in ~30m as config change in runtime. Edge FF needs small change in serialization, ~2-3h dev + deploy. Rollback would be immediate but requires rollout plan and coordination.

Customer Joe: Padding sounds fine as a temporary workaround — can you enable for my org? We're on enterprise plan.

Jamie S: @Maria L can you enable pad-first-chunk in europe-canary and then promote to europe-prod if green? I'll coordinate with Customer Joe for verification.

Maria L: On it. Creating feature flag + config:
```yaml
feature_flags:
  pad_first_stream_chunk: true  # runtime config, pad up to 128 bytes random
  pad_size_bytes: 96
```
Pushing canary now.

sre-bot: rollout: feature-flag pad_first_stream_chunk enabled in europe-canary (2025-12-09T14:52:11Z)

Chris H: watch logs for rq_8f3b2a family — packet captures show immediate first-chunk send after padding.

Maria L: Initial canary results: p99 TTFB in europe-canary dropped back to ~140ms after pad enabled. No impact on CPU observed so far for small traffic.

Jamie S: Great. Joe — can you verify on your side? If good we'll schedule prod rollout and backfill ticket to remove temp padding after we ship a proper framing-aware flush patch.

Customer Joe: Verified. TTFB back to normal for the sample requests. Thanks! :tada:

Maria L: Next steps (owners):
- Maria: implement serialization-aware flush in runtime to avoid proxy coalescing (remove need for padding) — ETA 2d
- Chris: run a broader sim across regions for different chunk sizes and proxy configs — ETA 1d
- Jamie: coordinate prod rollout of pad toggle and notify impacted customers — ETA 2h for rollout plan
- SRE: monitor p99 for 24h and be ready to rollback if any regressions show up.

Jamie S: I'll create an internal incident ticket and add customer notification template.

Customer Joe: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Please keep me posted in this thread.

Maria L: tagging plan: once runtime flush is ready we'll disable pad-first-chunk and release. We'll also add a telemetry check to alert when first-chunk size + framing header falls into coalesce-risk window.

sre-bot: alert: p99 TTFB europe-prod stable after canary promotion (2025-12-09T16:10:02Z)
